correctness.rationale: Reconstructed source Proposition 4.22 inverse return shells x_n=exp(1-(n+1)^delta). Because right first branch sends normalized uniform Y seeds to uniform [0,1], P(tau>n)=exp(1-(n+1)^delta), hence tau has exact floor((1+E)^(1/delta)) law with E~Exp(1). Integerization costs less than one per observation; true mean is asymptotically e Gamma(q+1) for q=1/delta. Tilted Z^q weights have a truncated Gamma(q+1,1) mass law, which concentrates at q with O(sqrt q) spread. For c<1 maxima lie below bq, c<b<1 while that truncated expectation mass→0; for c>1 truncate at bq with 1<b<c and variance ≤(bq)^q/(e^(cq)mu_q)→0, missing expectation→0. At c=1 cutoff q±q^(1/4) leaves half tilted mass below the cutoff, negligible middle mass, concentrated lower sum, and vanishing probability of any upper extreme. This proves deterministic critical 1/2 without assuming finite tests imply the triangular-array theorem. Independent Gamma CDF check at q=100,400,1600 gives at q .47344,.48671,.49335.
